To establish standards for creating strong passwords to protect company systems and data from unauthorized access.
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party users with access to company systems.

- Minimum length: 8 characters
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter
- Must contain at least one digit
- Special characters are optional but encouraged

- Maximum password age: 90 days
- Passwords must be changed every 90 days
- Password history: Remember last 5 passwords

- Maximum failed login attempts: 5
- Account lockout duration: 30 minutes
- Automatic unlock after lockout period

- Passwords must not be shared with anyone
- Passwords must not be written down or stored in plain text
- Use of password managers is encouraged but must be company-approved
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
- v1.0: Initial release (January 1, 2025)

**Effective Date:** July 1, 2025
**Supersedes:** v1.0
**Superseded By:** v3.0 (effective January 1, 2026)
To establish standards for creating strong passwords to protect company systems and data from unauthorized access.
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party users with access to company systems.

- Minimum length: 10 characters (increased from 8)
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter
- Must contain at least one digit
- Must contain at least one special character (!@#$%^&* etc.)

- Maximum password age: 60 days (reduced from 90 days)
- Passwords must be changed every 60 days
- Password history: Remember last 10 passwords (increased from 5)

- Maximum failed login attempts: 3 (reduced from 5)
- Account lockout duration: 45 minutes (increased from 30)
- Automatic unlock after lockout period
- After 3 lockouts in 24 hours, account requires IT unlock

- Passwords must not be shared with anyone
- Passwords must not be written down or stored in plain text
- Use of password managers is required for all administrative accounts
- Passwords must not be reused within 1 year

- MFA is required for all remote access
- MFA is required for all administrative accounts
- MFA is encouraged for all user accounts
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

- v1.0: Initial release (January 1, 2025)
- v2.0: Updated complexity and lockout requirements (July 1, 2025)

**Effective Date:** January 1, 2026
**Supersedes:** v2.0
**Superseded By:** None (current)
To establish standards for creating strong passwords to protect company systems and data from unauthorized access, aligning with NIST SP 800-63B and ISO 27001 requirements.
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, third-party users, and service accounts with access to company systems.

- Minimum length: 12 characters (increased from 10)
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter
- Must contain at least one digit
- Must contain at least two special characters from set: !@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}|;:,.<>?
- No dictionary words or common sequences (e.g., "password123", "qwerty")
- No context-specific words (company name, username, etc.)

- Maximum password age: 60 days (maintained from v2.0)
- Passwords must be changed every 60 days
- Password history: Remember last 24 passwords (increased from 10)
- Password reuse prohibited within 2 years

- Maximum failed login attempts: 3 (maintained from v2.0)
- Account lockout duration: 60 minutes (increased from 45)
- Automatic unlock after lockout period
- After 3 lockouts in 24 hours, account requires IT unlock and manager approval
- After 5 lockouts in 7 days, mandatory security training required

- Passwords must not be shared with anyone under any circumstances
- Passwords must not be written down or stored in plain text
- Use of company-approved password managers is required for all accounts
- Passwords must not be reused across different systems
- Passwords must not be used as answers to security questions

- MFA is required for all access (local, remote, and administrative)
- MFA methods must include at least two factors from: something you know (password), something you have (token/app), something you are (biometric)
- MFA cannot be disabled for any account
- Backup MFA methods must be configured and tested quarterly

- Passwords must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected
- All passwords must be changed upon employee termination or role change
- Service account passwords must be rotated every 90 days
- Passwords transmitted over networks must use encrypted channels (TLS 1.2+)
- Password storage must use approved hashing algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2) with salt

- Emergency access accounts require dual-control and weekly rotation
- Legacy systems unable to meet these requirements must be documented and isolated
- Exceptions require CISO approval and quarterly review

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
Automated compliance checking is performed weekly, with violations reported to management.

- v1.0: Initial release (January 1, 2025)
- v2.0: Updated complexity and lockout requirements (July 1, 2025)
- v3.0: NIST alignment, increased complexity, enhanced MFA requirements (January 1, 2026)

To establish a standardized approach for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents.
This procedure applies to all IT staff, security personnel, and employees who may encounter or report security incidents.

- Maintain incident response contact list (updated quarterly)
- Ensure backup and recovery procedures are tested monthly
- Conduct annual incident response tabletop exercises
- Maintain security monitoring tools in operational state

- Potential incidents reported via: security@company.com, ext. 5555, or ticketing system
- Initial triage within 15 minutes of report
- Severity levels: Low (informational), Medium (operational impact), High (data breach/risk), Critical (imminent threat)
- Evidence preservation: Collect logs, memory dumps, network captures

- Short-term: Isolate affected systems, block malicious IPs at firewall
- Long-term: Apply patches, change credentials, implement additional monitoring
- All containment actions documented and approved by incident lead

- Remove malware, close vulnerabilities, disable compromised accounts
- Verify eradication through scanning and monitoring
- Root cause analysis performed for all Medium+ severity incidents

- Return systems to production in controlled manner
- Validate functionality and security posture
- Monitor for recurrence for 30 days post-recovery
- Confirm with business owners before full restoration

- Incident report completed within 5 business days
- Meeting held within 2 weeks to review response effectiveness
- Update procedures, tools, or training based on findings
- Report distributed to management and relevant stakeholders

- **Incident Lead**: Overall coordination, decision-making, communication
- **Security Analyst**: Triage, evidence collection, analysis
- **Network Engineer**: Network containment, traffic analysis
- **System Administrator**: System isolation, patching, recovery
- **Legal Counsel**: Regulatory compliance, liability assessment
- **Public Relations**: External communications, breach notification
- **All Employees**: Report suspected incidents immediately

- Internal updates every 4 hours during active incident
- Status reports to management every 8 hours
- External notifications per regulatory requirements (within 72 hours for breaches)
- Post-incident summary distributed within 10 business days

- v1.0: Initial procedure (January 1, 2025)
- v1.1: Added containment timelines and roles clarification (March 15, 2025)

**Effective Date:** September 15, 2025
**Supersedes:** v1.1
**Superseded By:** v2.1 (effective March 1, 2026)
To establish a standardized approach for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents, aligned with NIST SP 800-61r2 and ISO 27035.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, and third parties with access to company information systems.

- Maintain incident response contact list (updated monthly)
- Ensure backup and recovery procedures are tested weekly
- Conduct quarterly incident response tabletop exercises
- Annual red team/blue team exercises
- Maintain security monitoring tools with 24/7 alerting

- Potential incidents reported via: security@company.com, ext. 5555, ticketing system, or mobile app
- Initial triage within 5 minutes of report (reduced from 15 minutes)
- Severity levels: 
  * Level 1: Informational (no action required)
  * Level 2: Low (documented, monitored)
  * Level 3: Medium (requires response within 4 hours)
  * Level 4: High (requires response within 1 hour)
  * Level 5: Critical (requires immediate response)
- Evidence preservation: Forensic images, memory dumps, network packets, logs
- Chain of custody documentation for all evidence

- Short-term: Network segmentation, account disabling, process termination
- Long-term: System rebuild, application patching, access control review
- All containment actions require dual approval for Critical incidents
- Automatic containment enabled for malware detected by EDR

- Complete removal of threat artifacts
- Vulnerability remediation within 24 hours for Critical incidents
- Root cause analysis using 5 Whys methodology
- Retesting of controls after eradication

- Systems restored from known good backups or rebuilt
- Validation in isolated environment before production return
- Monitoring for 45 days post-recovery (increased from 30)
- Business impact assessment conducted during recovery

- Formal incident report completed within 2 business days
- Lessons learned meeting within 5 business days
- Action items tracked in ticketing system with SLA
- Annual review of incident response program effectiveness
- Metrics: MTTD (Mean Time To Detect), MTTR (Mean Time To Respond), MTTC (Mean Time To Contain)

- **Incident Commander (IC)**: Overall authority, makes final decisions
- **Deputy IC**: Assists IC, manages specific aspects
- **Technical Lead**: Oversees technical response efforts
- **Communications Lead**: Internal and external communications
- **Documentation Lead**: Maintains records, chain of custody
- **Legal/Compliance**: Regulatory considerations, evidence handling
- **Business Liaison**: Represents affected business units
- **All Personnel**: Report incidents through designated channels immediately

- Status updates every hour during active incident (increased frequency)
- Executive briefings every 4 hours
- Regulatory notifications per applicable laws (GDPR: 72 hours, CCPA: 30 days)
- Internal breach notification to all employees within 24 hours for Confirmed breaches
- After-action report distributed to board of directors within 30 days

- Track: Number of incidents, MTTR, recurrence rate, false positives
- Monthly metrics report to security committee
- Quarterly effectiveness review
- Annual penetration test of IR capabilities

- v1.0: Initial procedure (January 1, 2025)
- v1.1: Added containment timelines and roles clarification (March 15, 2025)
- v2.0: NIST alignment, improved timelines, added metrics (September 15, 2025)

**Effective Date:** March 1, 2026
**Supersedes:** v2.0
**Superseded By:** None (current)
To establish a standardized approach for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents, incorporating lessons learned from recent threat landscape changes.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, third parties, and service accounts with access to company information systems.

- Maintain incident response contact list (updated weekly)
- Ensure backup and recovery procedures are tested weekly
- Conduct monthly incident response tabletop exercises (increased from quarterly)
- Annual red team/blue team exercises plus bi-annual purple team exercises
- Continuous monitoring of security tools with automated alert escalation

- Potential incidents reported via: security@company.com, ext. 5555, ticketing system, mobile app, or SIEM auto-creation
- Initial triage within 2 minutes of report (reduced from 5 minutes)
- Severity levels maintained but with updated response SLAs:
  * Level 1: Informational (logged, no action)
  * Level 2: Low (response within 8 hours)
  * Level 3: Medium (response within 2 hours) 
  * Level 4: High (response within 30 minutes)
  * Level 5: Critical (response within 5 minutes)
- Evidence preservation: Automated collection where possible, manual for complex cases
- Chain of custody: Blockchain-based evidence tracking system implemented

- Short-term: Automated isolation via SOAR playbooks, account disabling
- Long-term: Golden image restoration, zero-trust network segmentation
- Automatic containment enabled for all confirmed malicious activity
- Manual override available but requires dual approval and justification

- Complete removal using automated scripts where possible
- Vulnerability remediation: Critical within 4 hours, High within 24 hours
- Root cause analysis: Preliminary within 2 hours, detailed within 24 hours
- Validation of eradication through continuous monitoring

- Systems restored from immutable backups or rebuilt from gold images
- Validation includes security scanning and user acceptance testing
- Monitoring for 60 days post-recovery (increased from 45 days)
- Business continuity validation during recovery process

- Preliminary incident report within 1 business day
- Formal report and meeting within 3 business days (accelerated from v2.0)
- Action items assigned with automatic escalation if not completed
- Monthly IR effectiveness review with metrics trending
- Adoption of MITRE ATT&CK framework for technique tracking

- **Incident Commander (IC)**: Single point of authority during incident
- **Technical Operations Lead**: Manals technical response activities
- **Information Security Lead**: Ensures compliance with policies and regulations
- **Communications Lead**: Manages all internal and external messaging
- **Legal and Compliance Lead**: Handles regulatory notifications and evidence
- **Business Impact Lead**: Assesses and communicates business consequences
- **All Personnel**: Must report suspected incidents within 5 minutes of discovery (NEW REQUIREMENT)
- **Automated Systems**: Can initiate IR process without human intervention for certain threats

- Real-time status dashboard available to stakeholders
- Hourly updates during active incident via automated notifications
- Executive briefings every 2 hours during Critical incidents
- Regulatory notifications: As required by law, with attempt to notify within 24 hours where possible
- Internal notification: Secure alert sent to all employees for incidents affecting PII
- Post-incident review: Shared with entire organization for transparency (increased sharing)

- Enhanced metrics: 
  * MTTD: Target < 5 minutes
  * MTTR: Target < 2 hours for Medium incidents
  * MTTC: Target < 30 minutes for High incidents
  * percentage of incidents with automated response initiation
  * mean time to notify affected parties
- Real-time metrics dashboard
- Continuous improvement based on metrics analysis
- Annual third-party assessment of IR capabilities

- v1.0: Initial procedure (January 1, 2025)
- v1.1: Added containment timelines and roles clarification (March 15, 2025)
- v2.0: NIST alignment, improved timelines, added metrics (September 15, 2025)
- v2.1: Response time improvements, automation enhancements, stricter reporting (March 1, 2026)

To establish a framework for classifying company data based on its sensitivity and value to ensure appropriate protection measures are applied.
This policy applies to all data created, collected, processed, stored, or transmitted by the company, regardless of format or location.

- Definition: Information that can be freely shared with the public without harm
- Examples: Press releases, marketing materials, published financial reports
- Protection: No specific controls required beyond basic integrity
- Handling: Can be shared without restriction

- Definition: Information intended for company use only
- Examples: Internal memos, procedural documents, organizational charts
- Protection: Basic access controls, no encryption required for storage
- Handling: Share within company only, no external distribution

- Definition: Information that could cause harm if disclosed unauthorized
- Examples: Employee records, customer lists, financial projections
- Protection: Access controls, encryption required for transmission
- Handling: Need-to-know basis, confidentiality agreements for third parties

- Definition: Highly sensitive information requiring maximum protection
- Examples: Trade secrets, encryption keys, merger/acquisition details
- Protection: Strong access controls, encryption at rest and in transit, DLP
- Handling: Limited to specific individuals, strict usage monitoring

- **Data Owner**: Responsible for classifying data under their authority
- **Data Custodian**: Responsible for implementing security controls
- **All Employees**: Must classify data they create or handle according to guidelines
- **Data Stewards**: Assist with classification in large-scale implementations

- Public: No special requirements
- Internal: Company-approved systems
- Confidential: Access-controlled systems with logging
- Restricted: Encrypted storage, access logging, limited retention

- Public: No encryption required
- Internal: Company network acceptable
- Confidential: Encryption required for external transmission
- Restricted: Encryption required for all transmission, approved channels only

- All data must be destroyed according to retention schedules
- Confidential and Restricted data: Secure deletion methods required
- Certification of destruction for sensitive media

- Legal holds may override classification requirements
- Regulatory requirements may dictate specific handling
- Exceptions must be documented and approved by Information Security
- v1.0: Initial release (January 1, 2025)

**Effective Date:** September 1, 2025
**Supersedes:** v1.0
**Superseded By:** None (current)

To establish a comprehensive framework for classifying company data based on sensitivity, regulatory requirements, and business impact to ensure appropriate protection measures are applied consistently across the organization.

This policy applies to all data created, collected, processed, stored, or transmitted by the company, including data held by third parties on behalf of the company, regardless of format, location, or processing method.

- Definition: Information that is lawfully available to the general public from federal, state, or local government records
- Examples: Press releases, published financial statements, job postings, public website content
- Protection: Reasonable controls to prevent unauthorized modification; integrity protection recommended
- Handling: May be freely shared, distributed, or published without restriction

- Definition: Information intended for company use that is not sensitive but should not be unnecessarily disclosed
- Examples: Internal directories, policy documents, procedural manuals, organizational announcements
- Protection: Basic access controls (user authentication required); encryption not required for storage
- Handling: Share within company only; external sharing requires manager approval

- Definition: Information whose unauthorized disclosure could reasonably be expected to cause measurable harm to the company, employees, or customers
- Examples: Employee personnel records, customer lists, proprietary methodologies, internal financial reports
- Protection: Strong access controls (role-based); encryption required for transmission and recommended for storage
- Handling: Strict need-to-know basis; confidentiality agreements required for third-party access
- Retention: As per business and regulatory requirements

- Definition: Information whose unauthorized disclosure could cause severe harm, including legal penalties, significant financial loss, or irreparable reputation damage
- Examples: Trade secrets, encryption keys, merger/acquisition negotiations, security vulnerability details
- Protection: Maximum controls including segregation of duties, multi-factor authentication, encryption at rest and in transit, DLP, IRM
- Handling: Limited to specifically authorized individuals; detailed usage logging and monitoring
- Retention: Minimum necessary to fulfill business/legal requirements; secure destruction required

- Definition: Data subject to specific regulatory requirements that dictate handling, retention, and protection
- Examples: 
  * PII (Personally Identifiable Information) under GDPR/CCPA
  * PHI (Protected Health Information) under HIPAA
  * Financial data under PCI-DSS, SOX
  * Export-controlled information under EAR/ITAR
- Protection: As required by applicable regulations, which may exceed Restricted level controls
- Handling: As required by applicable regulations; specialized training may be required
- Retention: As required by applicable regulations

- **Data Owner**: Accountable for assessing and classifying data under their authority; reviews classification annually
- **Data Custodian**: Responsible for implementing and maintaining security controls for data in their care
- **Data Steward**: Assists with classification efforts, maintains classification registers, provides guidance
- **All Employees**: Must classify data they create or handle according to this policy; must complete annual training
- **Information Security Team**: Maintains classification framework, provides tools and guidance, handles exceptions

- Public: Company-approved systems with basic access controls
- Internal: Company-approved systems with user authentication
- Confidential: Access-controlled systems with logging; encryption recommended for storage
- Restricted: Encrypted storage with access logging; limited retention; air-gapped for highly sensitive subsets
- Special Categories: As required by applicable regulations

- Public: No encryption required for integrity protection
- Internal: Company network acceptable; encryption recommended for wireless transmission
- Confidential: Encryption required for all transmission outside trusted network
- Restricted: Encryption required for all transmission; approved secure channels only (SFTP, HTTPS, encrypted email)
- Special Categories: As required by applicable regulations

- Public: No restrictions
- Internal: Requires NDA or data processing agreement
- Confidential: Requires NDA and specific data handling commitments
- Restricted: Requires explicit approval and comprehensive data protection agreement
- Special Categories: As required by applicable regulations and data processing agreements

- All data must be destroyed according to documented retention schedules
- Public and Internal: Standard deletion procedures acceptable
- Confidential: Secure deletion methods (cryptographic wiping, physical destruction of media)
- Restricted and Special Categories: Physical destruction or certified cryptographic wiping required
- Certification of destruction required for all Confidential, Restricted, and Special Categories media

1. Inventory: Identify data elements and repositories
2. Assessment: Evaluate sensitivity, regulatory requirements, and business impact
3. Classification: Assign appropriate classification level(s)
4. Labeling: Apply classification labels where technically feasible
5. Protection: Implement appropriate security controls
6. Monitoring: Ongoing compliance monitoring and periodic review
7. Review: Classification reviewed annually or when significant changes occur

- Legal holds or litigation requirements may temporarily override classification requirements
- Regulatory inspections or audits may require specific handling
- Business process changes may necessitate classification review
- Formal exception process: Written request to Information Security with business justification, risk assessment, and mitigation plan
- Exceptions time-limited and subject to review; never granted for Restricted or Special Categories without compensating controls

- v1.0: Initial release (January 1, 2025)
- v2.0: Expanded classification levels, added Special Categories, formalized processes (September 1, 2025)

To define appropriate use of company technology resources and protect those resources from misuse, damage, or unauthorized access.

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporaries, and other workers at the company, including all personnel affiliated with third parties using company technology resources.
Company technology resources are provided for business use. Incidental personal use is permitted when it does not interfere with job performance, system operations, or other users.

- Accessing information and resources necessary for job performance
- Communication with colleagues, clients, and partners for business purposes
- Use of approved software and services for business tasks
- Limited personal use during breaks (email, web browsing, etc.)
- Training and professional development activities

- Any activity that violates local, state, federal, or international law
- Unauthorized access to computer systems (hacking)
- Distribution of viruses, malware, or other harmful code
- Copyright infringement or software piracy
- Possession or distribution of illegal materials

- Sharing passwords or authentication credentials
- Attempting to bypass security controls or monitoring
- Connecting unauthorized devices to the network
- Disabling or tampering with security software
- Attempting to access unauthorized systems or data

- Creating, accessing, or distributing obscene, pornographic, or sexually explicit material
- Creating, accessing, or distributing harassing, hateful, or discriminatory content
- Creating, accessing, or distributing defamatory or threatening content
- Engaging in cyberbullying or online harassment

- Excessive personal use that interferes with job responsibilities
- Running personal business activities using company resources
- Unauthorized use of company resources for political campaigns
- Streaming media or downloading large files that consume excessive bandwidth
- Cryptocurrency mining or other resource-intensive unauthorized activities

- Unauthorized copying, sharing, or removal of company data
- Sending confidential information via unsecured channels
- Using company resources to process personal data without authorization
- Violating data privacy policies or confidentiality agreements

- Company email systems are for business communication
- Professional and respectful tone required in all communications
- No expectation of privacy in company systems
- Monitoring may occur for security, maintenance, or policy compliance
- Automatic forwarding of company email to personal accounts prohibited

- Web browsing for business purposes permitted
- Access to job-related websites and resources encouraged
- Personal internet use permitted during designated breaks
- Web filtering may be employed to block inappropriate or malicious sites
- Downloading software requires IT approval and security scanning

- Company-issued mobile devices subject to same usage policies
- Personal devices used for company work must comply with BYOD policy
- Remote access must use approved secure methods (VPN, secure desktop)
- Company data on personal devices must be protected as if on company premises
- Lost or stolen devices must be reported immediately to IT security

- Personal social media use during work hours limited to breaks
- Company-affiliated social media accounts require authorization
- Employees must not represent themselves as speaking for the company without authorization
- Confidential company information must not be disclosed on social media
- Employees should be mindful of how personal posts reflect on their professional reputation

- Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination
- Illegal activities will be reported to law enforcement
- Company reserves right to examine any data stored on company systems
- Policy violations may result in loss of technology privileges

- v1.0: Initial policy (January 1, 2025)
- v1.1: Added social media and remote work sections (June 1, 2025)
- v1.2: Clarified prohibited activities and enforcement (February 1, 2025)

To define appropriate use of company technology resources, protect those resources from misuse, and ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and ethical standards in an evolving digital workplace.

This policy applies to all workforce members (employees, contractors, consultants, temporaries, volunteers, interns, and affiliates) and all company technology resources, including:
- Company-owned devices (desktops, laptops, mobile devices, servers)
- Personal devices used for company work (under BYOD policy)
- Company networks, systems, applications, and data
- Cloud services and third-party platforms used for company business
- Communication systems (email, messaging, video conferencing, telephony)
- Social media accounts representing the company
- Any technology resource accessing company data or networks

Company technology resources are provided primarily to support business operations. Limited incidental personal use is permitted when it:
- Does not interfere with job responsibilities or productivity
- Does not consume excessive system resources or bandwidth
- Does not violate any provision of this policy
- Does not expose the company to unnecessary risk or liability
- Occurs primarily during designated breaks or outside scheduled work hours

- Accessing information and resources necessary for job performance
- Communication with colleagues, clients, partners, and vendors for business purposes
- Use of company-approved software, services, and cloud platforms
- Limited personal communications and web browsing during breaks
- Online training, certification, and professional development activities
- Use of company resources for approved community service or volunteering
- Access to disability accommodations and assistive technologies as approved

- Any activity that violates applicable laws, regulations, or legal requirements
- Unauthorized access to computer systems, networks, or data (hacking)
- Creation, distribution, or use of malicious software (viruses, ransomware, spyware, etc.)
- Copyright infringement, software piracy, or violation of intellectual property rights
- Possession, creation, or distribution of illegal materials as defined by law
- Conducting illegal business activities using company resources

- Sharing passwords, PINs, biometric data, or other authentication credentials
- Attempting to bypass, disable, or circumvent security controls or monitoring
- Connecting unauthorized or unapproved devices to company networks
- Installing unauthorized software, hardware, or firmware on company devices
- Disabling, tampering with, or interfering with security software (antivirus, firewall, etc.)
- Attempting to access systems, networks, or data without proper authorization
- Introducing malicious code or conducting security testing without explicit authorization
- Physical tampering with company technology equipment

- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing harassing, intimidating, or threatening content
- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing discriminatory content based on protected characteristics
- Engaging in cyberbullying, online harassment, or creating hostile work environments digitally
- Using company resources to stalk, intimidate, or retaliate against individuals
- Creating or distributing content that creates a hostile work environment

- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing obscene, pornographic, or sexually explicit material
- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing excessively violent or graphic content
- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing content promoting illegal activities
- Creating, accessing, distributing, or storing content that could reasonably offend coworkers
- Engaging in sexting or sharing sexually suggestive content via company resources

- Excessive personal use that interferes with job responsibilities or duties
- Operating personal business activities or side hustles using company resources
- Unauthorized fundraising, solicitation, or political campaigning using company resources
- Streaming entertainment content, gaming, or other high-bandwidth personal activities
- Cryptocurrency mining, blockchain operations, or other resource-intensive computations
- Denial of service activities or attempts to overwhelm system resources
- Unauthorized use of company resources for external consulting or employment

- Unauthorized copying, sharing, transmission, or removal of company data
- Sending confidential or sensitive information via unsecured or unauthorized channels
- Using company resources to process, store, or transmit personal data without authorization
- Violating data privacy policies, confidentiality agreements, or data handling procedures
- Accessing, viewing, or distributing confidential information without business need
- Improper disposal or destruction of company data or media containing company data
- Attempting to conceal or obfuscate unauthorized activities

- Installing or using unlicensed, pirated, or unauthorized software
- Using software outside the scope of its license agreement
- Distributing company-licensed software to unauthorized individuals
- Modifying, reverse engineering, or tampering with licensed software
- Using company resources to develop software for personal or external use without approval

- Company email, messaging, and collaboration systems are for business communication
- Professional, respectful, and courteous communication expected in all interactions
- No reasonable expectation of privacy in company communication systems
- Monitoring may occur for security, maintenance, compliance, or investigative purposes
- Automatic forwarding of company email to personal accounts prohibited without approval
- Use of personal email accounts for company business requires authorization and compliance
- Retention of electronic communications as per applicable policies and legal requirements

- Web browsing for legitimate business purposes is permitted and encouraged
- Access to job-related websites, research resources, and professional networks supported
- Personal internet use permitted during designated breaks and outside work hours
- Web filtering and content controls may be employed to protect against threats
- Downloading files or software requires security scanning and may require IT approval
- Bandwidth-intensive activities may be limited or scheduled during off-peak hours
- Use of company resources for illegal file sharing or copyright infringement prohibited

- Subject to all provisions of this acceptable use policy
- May be monitored for security, compliance, and proper use
- Must be returned immediately upon termination or upon request
- Lost or stolen devices must be reported to IT security within one hour
- Personal use permitted but must comply with policy limitations

- Personal devices used for company work must be registered and approved
- Must comply with company security requirements (encryption, passwords, updates)
- Company may require installation of security profiles or management software
- Company data on personal devices must be protected as if on company premises
- Remote wipe capability may be enabled for lost/stolen devices or policy violations
- Separation of company and personal data recommended through containerization or profiles

- Remote access must use approved secure methods (VPN, zero-trust network access, etc.)
- Company data accessed remotely must be treated with same protections as onsite
- Home networks used for company work must meet minimum security standards
- Equipment used for remote work must be maintained in secure condition
- Ergonomic and safety considerations apply to home office setups

- Personal social media use during work hours limited to designated breaks
- Employees are personally responsible for content they post on personal accounts
- Personal posts should not interfere with job performance or workplace relationships
- Employees should be mindful of how personal activity reflects on professional reputation

- Creation and use of social media accounts representing the company requires authorization
- Authorized users must follow company branding, messaging, and engagement guidelines
- Confidential or non-public company information must not be disclosed on social media
- Political advocacy or personal opinions must not be presented as company positions
- Customer interactions on social media must follow company service guidelines

- Employees must not represent themselves as speaking for the company without authorization
- Confidential company information must not be disclosed on any social media platform
- Respectful and professional communication expected in all company-related interactions
- Harassment, discrimination, or retaliation via social media is prohibited
- Intellectual property considerations apply to content shared on social media

- Use of cloud services for company business requires appropriate authorization
- Must comply with company data classification and security requirements
- Data stored in third-party clouds must be protected according to its classification
- Terms of service and acceptable use policies of third parties must be reviewed
- Integration with company systems requires security review and approval
- Regular assessment of third-party security and compliance practices required

- Company reserves right to monitor, log, and review usage of technology resources
- Monitoring may include network traffic, system logs, email content, and file access
- Monitoring conducted for security, maintenance, policy compliance, or investigative purposes
- Investigations conducted in accordance with applicable laws and company policies
- Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination
- Illegal activities will be reported to appropriate law enforcement authorities
- Policy violations may result in loss of technology access privileges
- Repeated or severe violations may result in criminal or civil legal action

- This policy reviewed annually or as needed based on legal, technological, or business changes
- Updates communicated to all workforce members with appropriate training provided
- Version control maintained; superseded versions archived for reference
- Feedback on policy effectiveness and clarity encouraged and reviewed
